The voice would go to your heart. You would think the dear child was in trouble or in danger, and you couldn't rest without running to help her and comfort her.

reference: I'VE STRONG ASSURANCE THAT NO EVIL WILL HAPPEN TO YOU AND MY UNCLE AND THE CHILDREN FROM ANYTHING I'VE DONE
transcript: I've strong assurance that no evil will happen to you and my uncle and the children for many thing I have done.

reference: I DIDN'T PREACH WITHOUT DIRECTION
transcript: I didn't preach without direction.

reference: DIRECTION
transcript: Direction.

reference: I HANNA COMMON PATIENCE WITH YOU
transcript: I had a common patience with you.

reference: BY THIS TIME THE TWO GENTLEMEN HAD REACHED THE PALINGS AND HAD GOT DOWN FROM THEIR HORSES IT WAS PLAIN THEY MEANT TO COME IN
transcript: By this time, the two gentlemen had reached the palings and had got down from their horses. It was plain they meant to come in.

reference: SAID MISTER IRWINE WITH HIS STATELY CORDIALITY
transcript: Said Mr. Irwin, with his stately cordiality.

reference: OH SIR DON'T MENTION IT SAID MISSUS POYSER
transcript: Oh, sir, don't mention it, said Mrs. Poisoner.

reference: I DELIGHT IN YOUR KITCHEN
transcript: I delight in your kitchen.

reference: POYSER IS NOT AT HOME IS HE
transcript: Poisoner is not at home, is he?

reference: SAID CAPTAIN DONNITHORNE SEATING HIMSELF WHERE HE COULD SEE ALONG THE SHORT PASSAGE TO THE OPEN DAIRY DOOR
transcript: Said Captain Donny Thorne, sitting himself where he could see along the short passage to the open dairy-door

reference: NO SIR HE ISN'T HE'S GONE TO ROSSETER TO SEE MISTER WEST THE FACTOR ABOUT THE WOOL
transcript: No, sir, he isn't. He's gone to Rossiter to see Mr. West, the factor about the wall.

reference: BUT THERE'S FATHER THE BARN SIR IF HE'D BE OF ANY USE
transcript: But there's father in the barn, sir, if he'd be of any use.

reference: NO THANK YOU I'LL JUST LOOK AT THE WHELPS AND LEAVE A MESSAGE ABOUT THEM WITH YOUR SHEPHERD
transcript: No, thank you. I'll just look at the Welps and leave a message about them with your shepherd.

reference: I MUST COME ANOTHER DAY AND SEE YOUR HUSBAND I WANT TO HAVE A CONSULTATION WITH HIM ABOUT HORSES
transcript: I must come another day and see your husband. I want to have a consultation with him about horses.

reference: FOR IF HE'S ANYWHERE ON THE FARM WE CAN SEND FOR HIM IN A MINUTE
transcript: For if he's anywhere on the farm, we can send for him in a minute.

reference: OH SIR SAID MISSUS POYSER RATHER ALARMED YOU WOULDN'T LIKE IT AT ALL
transcript: Oh, sir, said Mrs. Poyser, rather alarmed. You wouldn't like it at all.

reference: BUT YOU KNOW MORE ABOUT THAT THAN I DO SIR
transcript: But you know more about that than I do, sir.

reference: I THINK I SHOULD BE DOING YOU A SERVICE TO TURN YOU OUT OF SUCH A PLACE
transcript: I think I should be doing you a service to turn you out of such a place.

reference: I KNOW HIS FARM IS IN BETTER ORDER THAN ANY OTHER WITHIN TEN MILES OF US AND AS FOR THE KITCHEN HE ADDED SMILING I DON'T BELIEVE THERE'S ONE IN THE KINGDOM TO BEAT IT
transcript: I know his farm is in better order than any other within ten miles of us, and as for the kitchen, he added, smiling, I don't believe there's one in the kingdom to beat it.

reference: BY THE BY I'VE NEVER SEEN YOUR DAIRY I MUST SEE YOUR DAIRY MISSUS POYSER
transcript: By the bye, I've never seen your dairy. I must see your dairy, Mrs. Poisoner.

reference: THIS MISSUS POYSER SAID BLUSHING AND BELIEVING THAT THE CAPTAIN WAS REALLY INTERESTED IN HER MILK PANS AND WOULD ADJUST HIS OPINION OF HER TO THE APPEARANCE OF HER DAIRY
transcript: This Mrs. Poyser said, blushing, and believing that the captain was really interested in her milk pans, and would adjust his opinion of her to the appearance of her dairy.

reference: OH I'VE NO DOUBT IT'S IN CAPITAL ORDER
transcript: Oh, I've no doubt it's in capital order.

reference: THE PARIS PLANT LIKE THAT AT THE CRYSTAL PALACE WAS A TEMPORARY EXHIBIT
transcript: The Paris plant, like that of the Crystal Palace, was a temporary exhibit.

reference: THE LONDON PLANT WAS LESS TEMPORARY BUT NOT PERMANENT SUPPLYING BEFORE IT WAS TORN OUT NO FEWER THAN THREE THOUSAND LAMPS IN HOTELS CHURCHES STORES AND DWELLINGS IN THE VICINITY OF HOLBORN VIADUCT
transcript: The London plant was less temporary, but not permanent, supplying before it was torn out, no fewer than three thousand lamps in hotels, churches, stores and dwellings in the vicinity of Holborn Viaduct.

reference: THERE MESSRS JOHNSON AND HAMMER PUT INTO PRACTICE MANY OF THE IDEAS NOW STANDARD IN THE ART AND SECURED MUCH USEFUL DATA FOR THE WORK IN NEW YORK OF WHICH THE STORY HAS JUST BEEN TOLD
transcript: There, Messrs Johnson and Hammer put into practice many of the ideas now standard in the art, and secured much useful data for the work in New York, of which the story has just been told.

reference: THE DYNAMO ELECTRIC MACHINE THOUGH SMALL WAS ROBUST FOR UNDER ALL THE VARYING SPEEDS OF WATER POWER AND THE VICISSITUDES OF THE PLANT TO WHICH IT BELONGED IT CONTINUED IN ACTIVE USE UNTIL EIGHTEEN NINETY NINE SEVENTEEN YEARS
transcript: The dynamo electric machine, though small, was robust for under all the varying speeds of water power and the vicissitudes of the plant to which it belonged, it continued in active use until eighteen ninety nine, seventeen years.

reference: OWING TO HIS INSISTENCE ON LOW PRESSURE DIRECT CURRENT FOR USE IN DENSELY POPULATED DISTRICTS AS THE ONLY SAFE AND TRULY UNIVERSAL PROFITABLE WAY OF DELIVERING ELECTRICAL ENERGY TO THE CONSUMERS EDISON HAS BEEN FREQUENTLY SPOKEN OF AS AN OPPONENT OF THE ALTERNATING CURRENT
transcript: Owing to his insistence on low pressure, direct current for use in densely populated districts as the only safe and truly universal profitable way of delivering electrical energy to the consumers, Edison has been frequently spoken of as an opponent of the alternating current.

reference: WHY IF WE ERECT A STATION AT THE FALLS IT IS A GREAT ECONOMY TO GET IT UP TO THE CITY
transcript: Why, if we erect a station at the falls, it is a great economy to get it up to the city.

reference: THERE SEEMS NO GOOD REASON FOR BELIEVING THAT IT WILL CHANGE
transcript: There seems no good reason for believing that it will change.

reference: BROAD AS THE PRAIRIES AND FREE IN THOUGHT AS THE WINDS THAT SWEEP THEM HE IS IDIOSYNCRATICALLY OPPOSED TO LOOSE AND WASTEFUL METHODS TO PLANS OF EMPIRE THAT NEGLECT THE POOR AT THE GATE
transcript: Brought as the prairies and free and thought as the winds that swept them, he is idiosyncratically opposed to loose and wasteful methods to plans of empire that neglect the poor at the gate.

reference: EVERYTHING HE HAS DONE HAS BEEN AIMED AT THE CONSERVATION OF ENERGY THE CONTRACTION OF SPACE THE INTENSIFICATION OF CULTURE
transcript: Everything he has done has been aimed at the conservation of energy, the contraction of space, the intensification of culture.

reference: FOR SOME YEARS IT WAS NOT FOUND FEASIBLE TO OPERATE MOTORS ON ALTERNATING CURRENT CIRCUITS AND THAT REASON WAS OFTEN URGED AGAINST IT SERIOUSLY
transcript: For some years it was not found feasible to operate motors on alternating current circuits, and that reason was often urged against it seriously.

reference: IT COULD NOT BE USED FOR ELECTROPLATING OR DEPOSITION NOR COULD IT CHARGE STORAGE BATTERIES ALL OF WHICH ARE EASILY WITHIN THE ABILITY OF THE DIRECT CURRENT
transcript: It could not be used for electroplating or deposition, nor could it charge storage batteries, all of which are easily within the ability of the direct current.

reference: BUT WHEN IT CAME TO BE A QUESTION OF LIGHTING A SCATTERED SUBURB A GROUP OF DWELLINGS ON THE OUTSKIRTS A REMOTE COUNTRY RESIDENCE OR A FARM HOUSE THE ALTERNATING CURRENT IN ALL ELEMENTS SAVE ITS DANGER WAS AND IS IDEAL
transcript: But when it came to be a question of lighting a scattered suburb, a group of dwellings on the outskirts, a remote country residence, or a farmhouse, the alternating currents in all elements, save its danger, was and is ideal.

reference: EDISON WAS INTOLERANT OF SHAM AND SHODDY AND NOTHING WOULD SATISFY HIM THAT COULD NOT STAND CROSS EXAMINATION BY MICROSCOPE TEST TUBE AND GALVANOMETER
transcript: Edison was intolerant of sham and shoddy, and nothing would satisfy him that could not stand cross-examination by microscope, test tube, and galvanometer.

reference: UNLESS HE COULD SECURE AN ENGINE OF SMOOTHER RUNNING AND MORE EXACTLY GOVERNED AND REGULATED THAN THOSE AVAILABLE FOR HIS DYNAMO AND LAMP EDISON REALIZED THAT HE WOULD FIND IT ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO GIVE A STEADY LIGHT
transcript: Unless he could secure an engine of smoother running and more exactly governed and regulated than those available for his dynamo and lamp, Edison realized that he would find it almost impossible to give a steady light.

reference: MISTER EDISON WAS A LEADER FAR AHEAD OF THE TIME
transcript: Mr. Edison was a leader far ahead of the time.

reference: HE OBTAINED THE DESIRED SPEED AND LOAD WITH A FRICTION BRAKE ALSO REGULATOR OF SPEED BUT WAITED FOR AN INDICATOR TO VERIFY IT
transcript: He obtained the desired speed and load with a friction break, also regulator of speed, but waited for an indicator to verify it.

reference: THEN AGAIN THERE WAS NO KNOWN WAY TO LUBRICATE AN ENGINE FOR CONTINUOUS RUNNING AND MISTER EDISON INFORMED ME THAT AS A MARINE ENGINE STARTED BEFORE THE SHIP LEFT NEW YORK AND CONTINUED RUNNING UNTIL IT REACHED ITS HOME PORT SO AN ENGINE FOR HIS PURPOSES MUST PRODUCE LIGHT AT ALL TIMES
transcript: Then again, there was no known way to lubricate an engine for continuous running, and Mr. Edison informed me that as a marine engine started before the ship left New York and continued running until it reached its home port, so an engine for his purposes must produce light at all times.

reference: EDISON HAD INSTALLED HIS HISTORIC FIRST GREAT CENTRAL STATION SYSTEM IN NEW YORK ON THE MULTIPLE ARC SYSTEM COVERED BY HIS FEEDER AND MAIN INVENTION WHICH RESULTED IN A NOTABLE SAVING IN THE COST OF CONDUCTORS AS AGAINST A STRAIGHT TWO WIRE SYSTEM THROUGHOUT OF THE TREE KIND
transcript: Edison had installed his historic first-grade central station system in New York on the multiple arc system covered by his feeder and maidenvention, which resulted in a notable saving in the cost of conductors as against a straight two-wire system throughout of the tree kind.

reference: HE SOON FORESAW THAT STILL GREATER ECONOMY WOULD BE NECESSARY FOR COMMERCIAL SUCCESS NOT ALONE FOR THE LARGER TERRITORY OPENING BUT FOR THE COMPACT DISTRICTS OF LARGE CITIES
transcript: He soon foresaw that still greater economy would be necessary for commercial success, not alone for the larger territory opening, but for the compact district of large cities.

reference: THE STRONG POSITION HELD BY THE EDISON SYSTEM UNDER THE STRENUOUS COMPETITION THAT WAS ALREADY SPRINGING UP WAS ENORMOUSLY IMPROVED BY THE INTRODUCTION OF THE THREE WIRE SYSTEM AND IT GAVE AN IMMEDIATE IMPETUS TO INCANDESCENT LIGHTING
transcript: The strong position held by the Edison system under the strenuous competition it was already springing up, was enormously improved by the introduction of the three wire system, and it gave an immediate impetus to incandescent lighting.

reference: IT WAS SPECIALLY SUITED FOR A TRIAL PLANT ALSO IN THE EARLY DAYS WHEN A YIELD OF SIX OR EIGHT LAMPS TO THE HORSE POWER WAS CONSIDERED SUBJECT FOR CONGRATULATION
transcript: It was specially suited for a trial plan also. In the early days, when a yield of six or eight lamps to the horsepower was considered subject for congratulation.

reference: THE STREET CONDUCTORS WERE OF THE OVERHEAD POLE LINE CONSTRUCTION AND WERE INSTALLED BY THE CONSTRUCTION COMPANY THAT HAD BEEN ORGANIZED BY EDISON TO BUILD AND EQUIP CENTRAL STATIONS
transcript: The street conductors were of the overhead pole line construction, and were installed by the construction company that had been organized by Edison to build and equip central stations.

reference: MEANWHILE HE HAD CALLED UPON ME TO MAKE A REPORT OF THE THREE WIRE SYSTEM KNOWN IN ENGLAND AS THE HOPKINSON BOTH DOCTOR JOHN HOPKINSON AND MISTER EDISON BEING INDEPENDENT INVENTORS AT PRACTICALLY THE SAME TIME
transcript: Meanwhile, he had called upon me to make a report of the three-wire system known in England as the Hopkinson, both Dr. John Hopkinson and Mr. Edison, being independent and venerous at practically the same time.

reference: I THINK HE WAS PERHAPS MORE APPRECIATIVE THAN I WAS OF THE DISCIPLINE OF THE EDISON CONSTRUCTION DEPARTMENT AND THOUGHT IT WOULD BE WELL FOR US TO WAIT UNTIL THE MORNING OF THE FOURTH BEFORE WE STARTED UP
transcript: I think he was perhaps more appreciative that I was of the discipline of the Edison construction department, and thought it would be well for us to wait until the morning of the fourth before we started up.

reference: BUT THE PLANT RAN AND IT WAS THE FIRST THREE WIRE STATION IN THIS COUNTRY
transcript: But the plant ran and it was the first three-wire station in this country.

reference: THEY WERE LATER USED AS RESERVE MACHINES AND FINALLY WITH THE ENGINE RETIRED FROM SERVICE AS PART OF THE COLLECTION OF EDISONIA BUT THEY REMAIN IN PRACTICALLY AS GOOD CONDITION AS WHEN INSTALLED IN EIGHTEEN EIGHTY THREE
transcript: They were later used as reserve machines, and finally, with the engine retired from service as part of the collection of Edisonia. But they remain in practically as good condition as one installed in eighteen eighty three.

reference: THE ARC LAMP INSTALLED OUTSIDE A CUSTOMER'S PREMISES OR IN A CIRCUIT FOR PUBLIC STREET LIGHTING BURNED SO MANY HOURS NIGHTLY SO MANY NIGHTS IN THE MONTH AND WAS PAID FOR AT THAT RATE SUBJECT TO REBATE FOR HOURS WHEN THE LAMP MIGHT BE OUT THROUGH ACCIDENT
transcript: The arc lamp installed outside a customer's premises, or in a circuit for public street lighting, burned so many hours nightly, so many nights in the month, and was paid for at that rate, subject to rebate for hours when the lamp might be out through accident.

reference: EDISON HELD THAT THE ELECTRICITY SOLD MUST BE MEASURED JUST LIKE GAS OR WATER AND HE PROCEEDED TO DEVELOP A METER
transcript: Edison held that the electricity sold must be measured just like gas or water, and he proceeded to develop a meter.

reference: THERE WAS INFINITE SCEPTICISM AROUND HIM ON THE SUBJECT AND WHILE OTHER INVENTORS WERE ALSO GIVING THE SUBJECT THEIR THOUGHT THE PUBLIC TOOK IT FOR GRANTED THAT ANYTHING SO UTTERLY INTANGIBLE AS ELECTRICITY THAT COULD NOT BE SEEN OR WEIGHED AND ONLY GAVE SECONDARY EVIDENCE OF ITSELF AT THE EXACT POINT OF USE COULD NOT BE BROUGHT TO ACCURATE REGISTRATION
transcript: There was infinite skepticism around him on the subject, and while other inventors were also giving the subject their thought, the public took it for granted that anything so utterly intangible as electricity that could not be seen or weighed, and only gave secondary evidence of itself at the exact point of use, could not be brought to accurate registration.

reference: HENCE THE EDISON ELECTROLYTIC METER IS NO LONGER USED DESPITE ITS EXCELLENT QUALITIES
transcript: Hence the Addison Electrolytic Meter is no longer used, despite its excellent qualities.

reference: THE PRINCIPLE EMPLOYED IN THE EDISON ELECTROLYTIC METER IS THAT WHICH EXEMPLIFIES THE POWER OF ELECTRICITY TO DECOMPOSE A CHEMICAL SUBSTANCE
transcript: The principle employed in the Addison electrolytic meter is that which exemplifies the power of electricity to decompose a chemical substance.

reference: ASSOCIATED WITH THIS SIMPLE FORM OF APPARATUS WERE VARIOUS INGENIOUS DETAILS AND REFINEMENTS TO SECURE REGULARITY OF OPERATION FREEDOM FROM INACCURACY AND IMMUNITY FROM SUCH TAMPERING AS WOULD PERMIT THEFT OF CURRENT OR DAMAGE
transcript: Associated with the simple form of apparatus were various ingenious details and refinements to secure regularity of operation, freedom from inaccuracy, and immunity from such tampering as would permit theft of current or damage.

reference: THE STANDARD EDISON METER PRACTICE WAS TO REMOVE THE CELLS ONCE A MONTH TO THE METER ROOM OF THE CENTRAL STATION COMPANY FOR EXAMINATION ANOTHER SET BEING SUBSTITUTED
transcript: The standard Edison meter practice was to remove the cells once a month to the meter room of the Central Station Company for examination. Another set being substituted.

reference: IN DECEMBER EIGHTEEN EIGHTY EIGHT MISTER W J JENKS READ AN INTERESTING PAPER BEFORE THE AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF ELECTRICAL ENGINEERS ON THE SIX YEARS OF PRACTICAL EXPERIENCE HAD UP TO THAT TIME WITH THE METER THEN MORE GENERALLY IN USE THAN ANY OTHER
transcript: In December, eighteen eighty eight, Mr. W. J. J. J. X read an interesting paper before the American Institute of Electrical Engineers on the six years of practical experience had up to that time with the meter, then more generally in use than any other.

reference: THE OTHERS HAVING BEEN IN OPERATION TOO SHORT A TIME TO SHOW DEFINITE RESULTS ALTHOUGH THEY ALSO WENT QUICKLY TO A DIVIDEND BASIS
transcript: The others having been in operation two short a time to show definite results, although they also went quickly to a dividend basis.

reference: IN THIS CONNECTION IT SHOULD BE MENTIONED THAT THE ASSOCIATION OF EDISON ILLUMINATING COMPANIES IN THE SAME YEAR ADOPTED RESOLUTIONS UNANIMOUSLY TO THE EFFECT THAT THE EDISON METER WAS ACCURATE AND THAT ITS USE WAS NOT EXPENSIVE FOR STATIONS ABOVE ONE THOUSAND LIGHTS AND THAT THE BEST FINANCIAL RESULTS WERE INVARIABLY SECURED IN A STATION SELLING CURRENT BY METER
transcript: In this connection, it should be mentioned that the association of Edison illuminating companies in the same year adopted resolutions unanimously to the effect that the Edison meter was accurate and that its use was not expensive for stations above 1,000 lights and that the best financial results were invariably secured in a station selling current by meter.

reference: THE METER CONTINUED IN GENERAL SERVICE DURING EIGHTEEN NINETY NINE AND PROBABLY UP TO THE CLOSE OF THE CENTURY
transcript: The meter continued in general service during eighteen ninety nine, and probably up to the close of the century.

reference: HE WEIGHED AND REWEIGHED THE METER PLATES AND PURSUED EVERY LINE OF INVESTIGATION IMAGINABLE BUT ALL IN VAIN
transcript: He weighed and rewaived the meter plates and pursued every line of investigation imaginable but all in vain.

reference: HE FELT HE WAS UP AGAINST IT AND THAT PERHAPS ANOTHER KIND OF A JOB WOULD SUIT HIM BETTER
transcript: He felt he was up against it, and that perhaps another kind of a job would suit him better.

reference: THE PROBLEM WAS SOLVED
transcript: The problem was solved.

reference: WE WERE MORE INTERESTED IN THE TECHNICAL CONDITION OF THE STATION THAN IN THE COMMERCIAL PART
transcript: We were more interested in the technical condition of the station than in the commercial part.

reference: WE HAD METERS IN WHICH THERE WERE TWO BOTTLES OF LIQUID
transcript: We had meters in which there were two bottles of liquid.

reference: HERE SHE WOULD STAY COMFORTED AND SOOTHED AMONG THE LOVELY PLANTS AND RICH EXOTICS REJOICING THE HEART OF OLD TURNER THE GARDENER WHO SINCE POLLY'S FIRST RAPTUROUS ENTRANCE HAD TAKEN HER INTO HIS GOOD GRACES FOR ALL TIME
transcript: Here she would stay, comforted and soothed among the lovely plants and rich exotics, rejoicing the heart of old Turner, the gardener, who, since Polly's first rapturous entrance, had taken her into his good graces for all time.

reference: EVERY CHANCE SHE COULD STEAL AFTER PRACTICE HOURS WERE OVER AND AFTER THE CLAMOROUS DEMANDS OF THE BOYS UPON HER TIME WERE FULLY SATISFIED WAS SEIZED TO FLY ON THE WINGS OF THE WIND TO THE FLOWERS
transcript: Every chance she could steal after practice hours were over, and after the clamorous demands of the boys upon her time were fully satisfied, was seized to fly on the wings of the wind to the flowers.

reference: THEN DEAR SAID MISSUS WHITNEY YOU MUST BE KINDER TO HER THAN EVER THINK WHAT IT WOULD BE FOR ONE OF YOU TO BE AWAY FROM HOME EVEN AMONG FRIENDS
transcript: Then dear, said Mrs. Whitney, you must be kinder to her than ever. Think what it would be for one of you to be away from home, even among friends.

reference: SOMEHOW OF ALL THE DAYS WHEN THE HOME FEELING WAS THE STRONGEST THIS DAY IT SEEMED AS IF SHE COULD BEAR IT NO LONGER
transcript: Somehow, of all the days when the home feeling was the strongest, this day it seemed as if she could bear it no longer.

reference: IF SHE COULD ONLY SEE PHRONSIE FOR JUST ONE MOMENT
transcript: The she could only see Francie for just one moment.

reference: OH SHE'S ALWAYS AT THE PIANO SAID VAN SHE MUST BE THERE NOW SOMEWHERE AND THEN SOMEBODY LAUGHED
transcript: Oh, she's always at the piano, said Van. She must be there now somewhere, and then somebody laughed.

reference: AT THIS THE BUNDLE OPENED SUDDENLY AND OUT POPPED PHRONSIE
transcript: At this, the bundle opened suddenly and out popped bronzy.

reference: BUT POLLY COULDN'T SPEAK AND IF JASPER HADN'T CAUGHT HER JUST IN TIME SHE WOULD HAVE TUMBLED OVER BACKWARD FROM THE STOOL PHRONSIE AND ALL
transcript: But Polly couldn't speak, and if Jasper hadn't caught her just in time, she would have tumbled over backward from the stool, fronzy and all.

reference: ASKED PHRONSIE WITH HER LITTLE FACE CLOSE TO POLLY'S OWN
transcript: Asked Bronzey, with her little face close to Polly's own.

reference: NOW YOU'LL STAY CRIED VAN SAY POLLY WON'T YOU
transcript: Now you'll stay, cried Van, say Polly, won't you?

reference: OH YOU ARE THE DEAREST AND BEST MISTER KING I EVER SAW BUT HOW DID YOU MAKE MAMMY LET HER COME
transcript: Oh, you are the dearest and best Mr. King I ever saw, but how did you make Mammy let her come?

reference: ISN'T HE SPLENDID CRIED JASPER IN INTENSE PRIDE SWELLING UP FATHER KNEW HOW TO DO IT
transcript: Isn't he splendid? cried Jasper, in intense pride, swelling up, Father knew how to do it.

reference: THERE THERE HE SAID SOOTHINGLY PATTING HER BROWN FUZZY HEAD
transcript: There, there, he said soothingly, patting her brown fuzzy head.

reference: I KNOW GASPED POLLY CONTROLLING HER SOBS I WON'T ONLY I CAN'T THANK YOU
transcript: I know, gasped Polly, controlling her sobs. I won't only. I can't thank you.

reference: ASKED PHRONSIE IN INTENSE INTEREST SLIPPING DOWN OUT OF POLLY'S ARMS AND CROWDING UP CLOSE TO JASPER'S SIDE
transcript: Asked Fronzy, in intense interest, slipping down out of Polly's arms and crowding up close to Jasper's side.

reference: YES ALL ALONE BY HIMSELF ASSERTED JASPER VEHEMENTLY AND WINKING FURIOUSLY TO THE OTHERS TO STOP THEIR LAUGHING HE DID NOW TRULY PHRONSIE
transcript: Yes, all alone by himself, asserted Jasper vehemently and winking furiously to the others to stop their laughing. He did now truly, Francie.

reference: OH NO JASPER I MUST GO BY MY VERY OWN SELF
transcript: Oh no, Jabster, I must go by my very own self.

reference: THERE JAP YOU'VE CAUGHT IT LAUGHED PERCY WHILE THE OTHERS SCREAMED AT THE SIGHT OF JASPER'S FACE
transcript: There, Jap, you've caught it, laughed Percy, while the others screamed at the sight of Jasper's face.

reference: DON'T MIND IT POLLY WHISPERED JASPER TWASN'T HER FAULT
transcript: Don't mind it, Polly, whispered Jasper, Twasnt her fault.

reference: DEAR ME EJACULATED THE OLD GENTLEMAN IN THE UTMOST AMAZEMENT AND SUCH A TIME AS I'VE HAD TO GET HER HERE TOO
transcript: Dear me, ejaculated, the old gentleman in the utmost amazement, and such a time as I've had to get her here, too.

reference: HOW DID HER MOTHER EVER LET HER GO
transcript: How did her mother ever let her go?

reference: SHE ASKED IMPULSIVELY I DIDN'T BELIEVE YOU COULD PERSUADE HER FATHER
transcript: She asked impulsively, I didn't believe you could persuade her father.

reference: I DIDN'T HAVE ANY FEARS IF I WORKED IT RIGHTLY SAID THE OLD GENTLEMAN COMPLACENTLY
transcript: I didn't have any fears if I worked it rightly, said the old gentleman complacently.

reference: HE CRIED IN HIGH DUDGEON JUST AS IF HE OWNED THE WHOLE OF THE PEPPERS AND COULD DISPOSE OF THEM ALL TO SUIT HIS FANCY
transcript: He cried and hide, dudgeon, just as if he owned the hole of the peppers, and could dispose of them all to suit his fancy.

reference: AND THE OLD GENTLEMAN WAS SO DELIGHTED WITH HIS SUCCESS THAT HE HAD TO BURST OUT INTO A SERIES OF SHORT HAPPY BITS OF LAUGHTER THAT OCCUPIED QUITE A SPACE OF TIME
transcript: And the old gentleman was so delighted with his success that he had to burst out into a series of short, happy bits of laughter that occupied quite a space of time.

reference: AT LAST HE CAME OUT OF THEM AND WIPED HIS FACE VIGOROUSLY
transcript: At last he came out of them and wiped his face vigorously.

reference: IT IS SIXTEEN YEARS SINCE JOHN BERGSON DIED
transcript: It is sixteen years since John Burks and died.

reference: HIS WIFE NOW LIES BESIDE HIM AND THE WHITE SHAFT THAT MARKS THEIR GRAVES GLEAMS ACROSS THE WHEAT FIELDS
transcript: His wife now lies beside him, and the white shaft that marks their graves gleams across the wheat-fields

reference: FROM THE NORWEGIAN GRAVEYARD ONE LOOKS OUT OVER A VAST CHECKER BOARD MARKED OFF IN SQUARES OF WHEAT AND CORN LIGHT AND DARK DARK AND LIGHT
transcript: From the Norwegian graveyard one looks out over a vast checkerboard marked off in squares of wheat and corn, light and dark, dark and light.

reference: FROM THE GRAVEYARD GATE ONE CAN COUNT A DOZEN GAYLY PAINTED FARMHOUSES THE GILDED WEATHER VANES ON THE BIG RED BARNS WINK AT EACH OTHER ACROSS THE GREEN AND BROWN AND YELLOW FIELDS
transcript: From the graveyard gate one can count a dozen gaily painted farmhouses, the gilded weather veins on the big red barns, wink at each other across the green and brown and yellow fields.

reference: THE AIR AND THE EARTH ARE CURIOUSLY MATED AND INTERMINGLED AS IF THE ONE WERE THE BREATH OF THE OTHER
transcript: The air and the earth are curiously mated and intermingled as if the one were the breath of the other.

reference: HE WAS A SPLENDID FIGURE OF A BOY TALL AND STRAIGHT AS A YOUNG PINE TREE WITH A HANDSOME HEAD AND STORMY GRAY EYES DEEPLY SET UNDER A SERIOUS BROW
transcript: He was a splendid figure of a boy, tall and straight as a young pine tree, with a handsome head and stormy gray eyes deeply set under a serious brow.

reference: THAT'S NOT MUCH OF A JOB FOR AN ATHLETE HERE I'VE BEEN TO TOWN AND BACK
transcript: That's not much of a job for an athlete here I've been to town and back.

reference: ALEXANDRA LETS YOU SLEEP LATE
transcript: Alexander, that's you sleep, laid.

reference: SHE GATHERED UP HER REINS
transcript: She gathered up her reins.

reference: PLEASE WAIT FOR ME MARIE EMIL COAXED
transcript: Please wait for me, Marie, Emil coaxed.

reference: I NEVER SEE LOU'S SCYTHE OVER HERE
transcript: I never see loose side over here.

reference: HOW BROWN YOU'VE GOT SINCE YOU CAME HOME I WISH I HAD AN ATHLETE TO MOW MY ORCHARD
transcript: How brown you've got since you came home? I wish I hadn't athlete to know my orchard.

reference: I GET WET TO MY KNEES WHEN I GO DOWN TO PICK CHERRIES
transcript: I get wet to mine knees when I go down to pick cherries.

reference: INDEED HE HAD LOOKED AWAY WITH THE PURPOSE OF NOT SEEING IT
transcript: Indeed, he had looked away with the purpose of not seeing it.

reference: THEY THINK YOU'RE PROUD BECAUSE YOU'VE BEEN AWAY TO SCHOOL OR SOMETHING
transcript: They think you're proud because you've been away to school or something.

reference: THERE WAS SOMETHING INDIVIDUAL ABOUT THE GREAT FARM A MOST UNUSUAL TRIMNESS AND CARE FOR DETAIL
transcript: There was something individual about the great farm, a most unusual trimness and care for detail.

reference: ON EITHER SIDE OF THE ROAD FOR A MILE BEFORE YOU REACHED THE FOOT OF THE HILL STOOD TALL OSAGE ORANGE HEDGES THEIR GLOSSY GREEN MARKING OFF THE YELLOW FIELDS
transcript: On either side of the road, for a mile before you reach the foot of the hill, stood tall, o sage, orange hedges, their glossy green, marking off the yellow fields.

reference: ANY ONE THEREABOUTS WOULD HAVE TOLD YOU THAT THIS WAS ONE OF THE RICHEST FARMS ON THE DIVIDE AND THAT THE FARMER WAS A WOMAN ALEXANDRA BERGSON
transcript: Any one thereabouts would have told you that this was one of the richest farms on the divide, and that the farmer was a woman, Alexandra Bergson.

reference: THERE IS EVEN A WHITE ROW OF BEEHIVES IN THE ORCHARD UNDER THE WALNUT TREES
transcript: There is even a white row of beehives in the orchard under the walnut-trees.

reference: FRANK READ ENGLISH SLOWLY AND THE MORE HE READ ABOUT THIS DIVORCE CASE THE ANGRIER HE GREW
transcript: Frank read English slowly, and the more he read about this divorce case, the angrier he grew.

reference: THIS DECISION WAS COMMUNICATED TO THE GIRLS
transcript: This decision was communicated to the girls.

reference: TABBY HAD TENDED THEM IN THEIR CHILDHOOD THEY AND NONE OTHER SHOULD TEND HER IN HER INFIRMITY AND AGE
transcript: Tabby had tended them in their childhood. They and none others should tend her in her infirmity in age.

reference: AT TEA TIME THEY WERE SAD AND SILENT AND THE MEAL WENT AWAY UNTOUCHED BY ANY OF THE THREE
transcript: At tea time, they were sad and silent, and the meal went away and touched by any of the three.

reference: SHE HAD ANOTHER WEIGHT ON HER MIND THIS CHRISTMAS
transcript: She had another weight on her mind this Christmas.

reference: BUT ANNE HAD BEGUN TO SUFFER JUST BEFORE THE HOLIDAYS AND CHARLOTTE WATCHED OVER HER YOUNGER SISTERS WITH THE JEALOUS VIGILANCE OF SOME WILD CREATURE THAT CHANGES HER VERY NATURE IF DANGER THREATENS HER YOUNG
transcript: But Anne had begun to suffer just before the holidays, and Charlotte watched over her younger sisters with a jealous vigilance of some wild creature that changes her very nature if danger threatens her young.

reference: STUNG BY ANXIETY FOR THIS LITTLE SISTER SHE UPBRAIDED MISS W FOR HER FANCIED INDIFFERENCE TO ANNE'S STATE OF HEALTH
transcript: Stung by anxiety for this little sister, she upbraided Miss W for her fancied indifference to Anstead of Health.

reference: STILL HER HEART HAD RECEIVED A SHOCK IN THE PERCEPTION OF ANNE'S DELICACY AND ALL THESE HOLIDAYS SHE WATCHED OVER HER WITH THE LONGING FOND ANXIETY WHICH IS SO FULL OF SUDDEN PANGS OF FEAR
transcript: Still, her heart had received a shock in the perception of Anne's delicacy, and all these holidays she watched over her with the longing fawn anxiety, which is so full of sudden pangs of fear.

reference: I DOUBT WHETHER BRANWELL WAS MAINTAINING HIMSELF AT THIS TIME
transcript: I doubt whether Branwell was maintaining himself at this time.

reference: TO CELEBRATE THE ARRIVAL OF HER SON SILVIA GAVE A SPLENDID SUPPER TO WHICH SHE HAD INVITED ALL HER RELATIVES AND IT WAS A GOOD OPPORTUNITY FOR ME TO MAKE THEIR ACQUAINTANCE
transcript: To celebrate the arrival of her son, Sylvia gave a splendid supper to which she had invited all her relatives, and it was a good opportunity for me to make their acquaintance.

reference: WITHOUT SAYING IT POSITIVELY SHE MADE ME UNDERSTAND THAT BEING HERSELF AN ILLUSTRIOUS MEMBER OF THE REPUBLIC OF LETTERS SHE WAS WELL AWARE THAT SHE WAS SPEAKING TO AN INSECT
transcript: Without saying it positively, she made me understand that being herself and illustrious member of the Republic of Letters, she was well aware that she was speaking to an insect.

reference: IN ORDER TO PLEASE HER I SPOKE TO HER OF THE ABBE CONTI AND I HAD OCCASION TO QUOTE TWO LINES OF THAT PROFOUND WRITER
transcript: In order to please her, I spoke to her of the Abbey Conti, and I had occasion to quote two lines of that profound writer.

reference: MADAM CORRECTED ME WITH A PATRONIZING AIR FOR MY PRONUNCIATION OF THE WORD SCEVRA WHICH MEANS DIVIDED SAYING THAT IT OUGHT TO BE PRONOUNCED SCEURA AND SHE ADDED THAT I OUGHT TO BE VERY GLAD TO HAVE LEARNED SO MUCH ON THE FIRST DAY OF MY ARRIVAL IN PARIS TELLING ME THAT IT WOULD BE AN IMPORTANT DAY IN MY LIFE
transcript: Madame corrected me with a patronizing air for my pronunciation of the word scavra, which means divided, saying that it ought to be pronounced, scura, and she added that I ought to be very glad to have learned so much on the first day of my arrival in Paris, telling me that it would be an important day in my life.

reference: HER FACE WAS AN ENIGMA FOR IT INSPIRED EVERYONE WITH THE WARMEST SYMPATHY AND YET IF YOU EXAMINED IT ATTENTIVELY THERE WAS NOT ONE BEAUTIFUL FEATURE SHE COULD NOT BE CALLED HANDSOME BUT NO ONE COULD HAVE THOUGHT HER UGLY
transcript: Her face was an enigma, for it inspired everyone with the warmest sympathy, and yet, if you examined it attentively, there was not one beautiful feature. She could not be called handsome, but no one could have thought her ugly.

reference: SILVIA WAS THE ADORATION OF FRANCE AND HER TALENT WAS THE REAL SUPPORT OF ALL THE COMEDIES WHICH THE GREATEST AUTHORS WROTE FOR HER ESPECIALLY OF THE PLAYS OF MARIVAUX FOR WITHOUT HER HIS COMEDIES WOULD NEVER HAVE GONE TO POSTERITY
transcript: Sylvia was the adoration of France, and her talent was the real support of all the comedies which the greatest authors wrote for her, especially of the plays of Mariovo, for without her, his comedies would never have gone to posterity.

reference: SILVIA DID NOT THINK THAT HER GOOD CONDUCT WAS A MERIT FOR SHE KNEW THAT SHE WAS VIRTUOUS ONLY BECAUSE HER SELF LOVE COMPELLED HER TO BE SO AND SHE NEVER EXHIBITED ANY PRIDE OR ASSUMED ANY SUPERIORITY TOWARDS HER THEATRICAL SISTERS ALTHOUGH SATISFIED TO SHINE BY THEIR TALENT OR THEIR BEAUTY THEY CARED LITTLE ABOUT RENDERING THEMSELVES CONSPICUOUS BY THEIR VIRTUE
transcript: Sylvia did not think that her good conduct was a merit, for she knew that she was virtuous only because herself loved compelled her to be so, and she never exhibited any pride or assumed any superiority towards her theatrical sisters, although satisfied to shine by their talent or their beauty, they cared little about rendering themselves conspicuous by their virtue.

reference: TWO YEARS BEFORE HER DEATH I SAW HER PERFORM THE CHARACTER OF MARIANNE IN THE COMEDY OF MARIVAUX AND IN SPITE OF HER AGE AND DECLINING HEALTH THE ILLUSION WAS COMPLETE
transcript: Two years before her death, I saw her perform the character of Marianne in the comedy of Maravot, an in spite of her age and declining health, the illusion was complete.

reference: SHE WAS HONOURABLY BURIED IN THE CHURCH OF SAINT SAUVEUR WITHOUT THE SLIGHTEST OPPOSITION FROM THE VENERABLE PRIEST WHO FAR FROM SHARING THE ANTI CHRISTAIN INTOLERANCY OF THE CLERGY IN GENERAL SAID THAT HER PROFESSION AS AN ACTRESS HAD NOT HINDERED HER FROM BEING A GOOD CHRISTIAN AND THAT THE EARTH WAS THE COMMON MOTHER OF ALL HUMAN BEINGS AS JESUS CHRIST HAD BEEN THE SAVIOUR OF ALL MANKIND
transcript: She was honorably buried in the Church of Saint Severe. Without the slightest opposition from the venerable priest, who, far from sharing the anti-Christian intolerancy of the clergy in general, said that her profession as an actress had not hindered her from being a good Christian, and that the earth was a common mother of all human beings, as Jesus Christ had been the saviour of all mankind.

reference: YOU WILL FORGIVE ME DEAR READER IF I HAVE MADE YOU ATTEND THE FUNERAL OF SILVIA TEN YEARS BEFORE HER DEATH BELIEVE ME I HAVE NO INTENTION OF PERFORMING A MIRACLE YOU MAY CONSOLE YOURSELF WITH THE IDEA THAT I SHALL SPARE YOU THAT UNPLEASANT TASK WHEN POOR SILVIA DIES
transcript: You will forgive me, dear reader, if I have made you attend the funeral of Sylvia ten years before her death. Believe me, I have no intention of performing a miracle. You may console yourself with the idea that I shall spare you that unpleasant task when poor Sylvia dies.

reference: I NEVER HAD ANY FAMILY
transcript: I never had any family.

reference: I HAD A NAME I BELIEVE IN MY YOUNG DAYS BUT I HAVE FORGOTTEN IT SINCE I HAVE BEEN IN SERVICE
transcript: I had a name I believe in my young days, but I have forgotten it since I have been in service.

reference: I SHALL CALL YOU ESPRIT
transcript: I shall call you a spree

reference: YOU DO ME A GREAT HONOUR
transcript: You do me a great honour.

reference: HERE GO AND GET ME CHANGE FOR A LOUIS I HAVE IT SIR
transcript: Here, go and get me change for a Louis. I have it, sir.

reference: AT YOUR SERVICE SIR
transcript: At your service, sir.

reference: MADAME QUINSON BESIDES CAN ANSWER YOUR ENQUIRIES
transcript: Madame Quinsong, besides, can answer your inquiries.

reference: I SEE A QUANTITY OF CHAIRS FOR HIRE AT THE RATE OF ONE SOU MEN READING THE NEWSPAPER UNDER THE SHADE OF THE TREES GIRLS AND MEN BREAKFASTING EITHER ALONE OR IN COMPANY WAITERS WHO WERE RAPIDLY GOING UP AND DOWN A NARROW STAIRCASE HIDDEN UNDER THE FOLIAGE
transcript: I see a quantity of chairs for hire at the rate of one Sioux, men reading the newspaper under the shade of the trees, girls and men breakfasting either alone or in company, waiters who were rapidly going up and down a narrow staircase hidden under the foliage.

reference: I SIT DOWN AT A SMALL TABLE A WAITER COMES IMMEDIATELY TO ENQUIRE MY WISHES
transcript: I sit down at a small table. A waiter comes immediately to inquire my wishes.

reference: I TELL HIM TO GIVE ME SOME COFFEE IF IT IS GOOD
transcript: I tell him to give me some coffee if it is good.

reference: THEN TURNING TOWARDS ME HE SAYS THAT I LOOK LIKE A FOREIGNER AND WHEN I SAY THAT I AM AN ITALIAN HE BEGINS TO SPEAK TO ME OF THE COURT OF THE CITY OF THE THEATRES AND AT LAST HE OFFERS TO ACCOMPANY ME EVERYWHERE
transcript: Then, turning towards me, he says that I look like a foreigner, and when I say that I am an Italian, he begins to speak to me of the court, the city of the theatres, and at last he offers to accompany me everywhere.

reference: I THANK HIM AND TAKE MY LEAVE
transcript: I thank him and take my leave.

reference: I ADDRESS HIM IN ITALIAN AND HE ANSWERS VERY WITTILY BUT HIS WAY OF SPEAKING MAKES ME SMILE AND I TELL HIM WHY
transcript: I address him in Italian, and he answers very whitily, but his way of speaking makes me smile, and I tell him why.

reference: MY REMARK PLEASES HIM BUT I SOON PROVE TO HIM THAT IT IS NOT THE RIGHT WAY TO SPEAK HOWEVER PERFECT MAY HAVE BEEN THE LANGUAGE OF THAT ANCIENT WRITER
transcript: My remark pleases him, but I soon prove to him that it is not the right way to speak. However, Perfect may have been the language of that ancient writer.

reference: I SEE A CROWD IN ONE CORNER OF THE GARDEN EVERYBODY STANDING STILL AND LOOKING UP
transcript: I see a crowd in one corner of the garden. Everybody standing still and looking up.

reference: IS THERE NOT A MERIDIAN EVERYWHERE
transcript: Is there not a meridian everywhere?

reference: YES BUT THE MERIDIAN OF THE PALAIS ROYAL IS THE MOST EXACT
transcript: Yes, but the meridian of the Palais Royal is the most exact.

reference: THAT IS TRUE BADAUDERIE
transcript: That is true bad dog bree

reference: ALL THESE HONEST PERSONS ARE WAITING THEIR TURN TO GET THEIR SNUFF BOXES FILLED
transcript: All these honest persons are waiting their turn to get their snuff boxes filled.

reference: IT IS SOLD EVERYWHERE BUT FOR THE LAST THREE WEEKS NOBODY WILL USE ANY SNUFF BUT THAT SOLD AT THE CIVET CAT
transcript: It is sold everywhere, but for the last three weeks nobody will use any snuff but that sold at the Sevette cat.

reference: IS IT BETTER THAN ANYWHERE ELSE
transcript: Is it better than anywhere else?

reference: BUT HOW DID SHE MANAGE TO RENDER IT SO FASHIONABLE
transcript: But how did she manage to render it so fashionable?

reference: SIMPLY BY STOPPING HER CARRIAGE TWO OR THREE TIMES BEFORE THE SHOP TO HAVE HER SNUFF BOX FILLED AND BY SAYING ALOUD TO THE YOUNG GIRL WHO HANDED BACK THE BOX THAT HER SNUFF WAS THE VERY BEST IN PARIS
transcript: Simply by stopping her carriage two or three times before the shop to have her snuff box filled, and by saying aloud to the young girl who handed back the box that her snuff was the very best in Paris.

reference: YOU ARE NOW IN THE ONLY COUNTRY IN THE WORLD WHERE WIT CAN MAKE A FORTUNE BY SELLING EITHER A GENUINE OR A FALSE ARTICLE IN THE FIRST CASE IT RECEIVES THE WELCOME OF INTELLIGENT AND TALENTED PEOPLE AND IN THE SECOND FOOLS ARE ALWAYS READY TO REWARD IT FOR SILLINESS IS TRULY A CHARACTERISTIC OF THE PEOPLE HERE AND HOWEVER WONDERFUL IT MAY APPEAR SILLINESS IS THE DAUGHTER OF WIT
transcript: You are now in the only country in the world where wit can make a fortune by selling either a genuine or a false article. In the first case, it receives the welcome of intelligent and talented people. And in the second, fools are always ready to reward it. For silliness is truly a characteristic of the people here, and however wonderful it may appear, silliness is the daughter of wit.

reference: LET A MAN RUN AND EVERYBODY WILL RUN AFTER HIM THE CROWD WILL NOT STOP UNLESS THE MAN IS PROVED TO BE MAD BUT TO PROVE IT IS INDEED A DIFFICULT TASK BECAUSE WE HAVE A CROWD OF MEN WHO MAD FROM THEIR BIRTH ARE STILL CONSIDERED WISE
transcript: Let a man run, and everybody will run after him. The crowd will not stop unless the man is proved to be mad, but to prove it is indeed a difficult task, because we have a crowd of men who, mad from their birth, are still considered wise.

reference: IT SEEMS TO ME I REPLIED THAT SUCH APPROVAL SUCH RATIFICATION OF THE OPINION EXPRESSED BY THE KING THE PRINCES OF THE BLOOD ET CETERA IS RATHER A PROOF OF THE AFFECTION FELT FOR THEM BY THE NATION FOR THE FRENCH CARRY THAT AFFECTION TO SUCH AN EXTENT THAT THEY BELIEVE THEM INFALLIBLE
transcript: It seems to me, I replied, that such approval, such ratification of the opinion expressed by the King, the princes of the blood, etc, is rather a proof of the affection felt for them by the nation, for the French carry that affection to such an extent that they believe them infallible.

reference: WHEN THE KING COMES TO PARIS EVERYBODY CALLS OUT VIVE LE ROI
transcript: When the king comes to Paris, everybody calls out "Vivilaroi".

reference: SHE INTRODUCED ME TO ALL HER GUESTS AND GAVE ME SOME PARTICULARS RESPECTING EVERY ONE OF THEM
transcript: She introduced me to all her guests and gave me some particulars respecting every one of them.

reference: WHAT SIR I SAID TO HIM AM I FORTUNATE ENOUGH TO SEE YOU
transcript: What sir, I said to him, am I fortunate enough to see you?

reference: HE HIMSELF RECITED THE SAME PASSAGE IN FRENCH AND POLITELY POINTED OUT THE PARTS IN WHICH HE THOUGHT THAT I HAD IMPROVED ON THE ORIGINAL
transcript: He himself recited the same passage in French, and politely pointed out the parts in which he thought that I had improved on the original.

reference: FOR THE FIRST DAY SIR I THINK THAT WHAT YOU HAVE DONE GIVES GREAT HOPES OF YOU AND WITHOUT ANY DOUBT YOU WILL MAKE RAPID PROGRESS
transcript: For the first day, sir, I think that what you have done gives great hopes of you, and without any doubt you will make rapid progress.

reference: I BELIEVE IT SIR AND THAT IS WHAT I FEAR THEREFORE THE PRINCIPAL OBJECT OF MY VISIT HERE IS TO DEVOTE MYSELF ENTIRELY TO THE STUDY OF THE FRENCH LANGUAGE
transcript: I believe it, sir, and that is what I fear. Therefore, the principal object of my visit here is to devote myself entirely to the study of the French language.

reference: I AM A VERY UNPLEASANT PUPIL ALWAYS ASKING QUESTIONS CURIOUS TROUBLESOME INSATIABLE AND EVEN SUPPOSING THAT I COULD MEET WITH THE TEACHER I REQUIRE I AM AFRAID I AM NOT RICH ENOUGH TO PAY HIM
transcript: I am a very unpleasant pupil, always asking questions, curious, troublesome, insatiable, and even supposing that I could meet with the teacher I require, I am afraid I am not rich enough to pay him.

reference: I RESIDE IN THE MARAIS RUE DE DOUZE PORTES
transcript: I reside in the mafia Grudidus port.

reference: I WILL MAKE YOU TRANSLATE THEM INTO FRENCH AND YOU NEED NOT BE AFRAID OF MY FINDING YOU INSATIABLE
transcript: I will make you translate them into French, and you need not be afraid of my finding you insatiable.

reference: HE HAD A GOOD APPETITE COULD TELL A GOOD STORY WITHOUT LAUGHING WAS CELEBRATED FOR HIS WITTY REPARTEES AND HIS SOCIABLE MANNERS BUT HE SPENT HIS LIFE AT HOME SELDOM GOING OUT AND SEEING HARDLY ANYONE BECAUSE HE ALWAYS HAD A PIPE IN HIS MOUTH AND WAS SURROUNDED BY AT LEAST TWENTY CATS WITH WHICH HE WOULD AMUSE HIMSELF ALL DAY
transcript: He had a good appetite, could tell a good story without laughing, was celebrated for his witty repartees and his sociable manners, but he spent his life at home, seldom going out and seeing hardly anyone, because he always had a pipe in his mouth and was surrounded by at least twenty cats with which he would amuse himself all day.

reference: HIS HOUSEKEEPER HAD THE MANAGEMENT OF EVERYTHING SHE NEVER ALLOWED HIM TO BE IN NEED OF ANYTHING AND SHE GAVE NO ACCOUNT OF HIS MONEY WHICH SHE KEPT ALTOGETHER BECAUSE HE NEVER ASKED HER TO RENDER ANY ACCOUNTS
transcript: His housekeeper had the management of everything. She never allowed him to be in need of anything, and she gave no account of his money, which she kept altogether because he never asked her to render any accounts.

reference: ON THE SIXTH OF APRIL EIGHTEEN THIRTY THE CHURCH OF JESUS CHRIST OF LATTER DAY SAINTS WAS FORMALLY ORGANIZED AND THUS TOOK ON A LEGAL EXISTENCE
transcript: On the sixth of April, eighteen thirty, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints was formerly organized and thus took on a legal existence.

reference: ITS ORIGIN WAS SMALL A GERM AN INSIGNIFICANT SEED HARDLY TO BE THOUGHT OF AS LIKELY TO AROUSE OPPOSITION
transcript: Its origin was small, a germ, an insignificant seed, hardly to be thought of as likely to arouse opposition.

reference: INSTEAD OF BUT SIX REGULARLY AFFILIATED MEMBERS AND AT MOST TWO SCORE OF ADHERENTS THE ORGANIZATION NUMBERS TODAY MANY HUNDRED THOUSAND SOULS
transcript: Instead of but six regularly affiliated members, and at most two score of adherents, the organization numbers today many hundred thousand souls.

reference: IN PLACE OF A SINGLE HAMLET IN THE SMALLEST CORNER OF WHICH THE MEMBERS COULD HAVE CONGREGATED THERE NOW ARE ABOUT SEVENTY STAKES OF ZION AND ABOUT SEVEN HUNDRED ORGANIZED WARDS EACH WARD AND STAKE WITH ITS FULL COMPLEMENT OF OFFICERS AND PRIESTHOOD ORGANIZATIONS
transcript: In place have a single hamlet, in the smallest corner of which the members could have congregated. There now are about seventy stakes of Zion and about seven hundred organized wards, each ward and stake with its full complement of officers and preset organizations.

reference: THE PRACTISE OF GATHERING ITS PROSELYTES INTO ONE PLACE PREVENTS THE BUILDING UP AND STRENGTHENING OF FOREIGN BRANCHES AND INASMUCH AS EXTENSIVE AND STRONG ORGANIZATIONS ARE SELDOM MET WITH ABROAD VERY ERRONEOUS IDEAS EXIST CONCERNING THE STRENGTH OF THE CHURCH
transcript: The practice of gathering its proselytes into one place prevents the billing up and strengthening of foreign branches, and inasmuch as extensive and strong organizations are seldom met with abroad, very erroneous ideas exist concerning the strength of the church.

reference: NEVERTHELESS THE MUSTARD SEED AMONG THE SMALLEST OF ALL SEEDS HAS ATTAINED THE PROPORTIONS OF A TREE AND THE BIRDS OF THE AIR ARE NESTING IN ITS BRANCHES THE ACORN IS NOW AN OAK OFFERING PROTECTION AND THE SWEETS OF SATISFACTION TO EVERY EARNEST PILGRIM JOURNEYING ITS WAY FOR TRUTH
transcript: Nevertheless, the mustard seed among the smallest of all seeds has attained the proportions of a tree, and the birds of the air are nesting in its branches. The acorn is now in oak, offering protection and the sweets of satisfaction to every earnest pilgrim journeying its way for truth.

reference: THEIR EYES WERE FROM THE FIRST TURNED IN ANTICIPATION TOWARD THE EVENING SUN NOT MERELY THAT THE WORK OF PROSELYTING SHOULD BE CARRIED ON IN THE WEST BUT THAT THE HEADQUARTERS OF THE CHURCH SHOULD BE THERE ESTABLISHED
transcript: Their eyes were from the first turned in anticipation toward the evening sun. Not merely that the work of proselyting should be carried on in the west, but that the headquarters of the church should be there established.

reference: THE BOOK OF MORMON HAD TAUGHT THE PEOPLE THE TRUE ORIGIN AND DESTINY OF THE AMERICAN INDIANS AND TOWARD THIS DARK SKINNED REMNANT OF A ONCE MIGHTY PEOPLE THE MISSIONARIES OF MORMONISM EARLY TURNED THEIR EYES AND WITH THEIR EYES WENT THEIR HEARTS AND THEIR HOPES
transcript: The Book of Mormon had taught the people the true origin and destiny of the American Indians, and toward this dark-skinned remnant of a once mighty people, the missionaries of Mormonism early turned their eyes, and with their eyes went their hearts and their hopes.

reference: IT IS NOTABLE THAT THE INDIAN TRIBES HAVE GENERALLY REGARDED THE RELIGION OF THE LATTER DAY SAINTS WITH FAVOR SEEING IN THE BOOK OF MORMON STRIKING AGREEMENT WITH THEIR OWN TRADITIONS
transcript: It is notable that the Indian tribes have generally regarded their religion of the Latter-day Saints with favor, seeing in the Book of Mormon striking agreement with their own traditions.

reference: THE FIRST WELL ESTABLISHED SEAT OF THE CHURCH WAS IN THE PRETTY LITTLE TOWN OF KIRTLAND OHIO ALMOST WITHIN SIGHT OF LAKE ERIE AND HERE SOON ROSE THE FIRST TEMPLE OF MODERN TIMES
transcript: The first well established seat of the church was in the pretty little town of Curland, Ohio, almost within sight of Lake Erie, and here soon rose the first temple of modern times.

reference: TO THE FERVENT LATTER DAY SAINT A TEMPLE IS NOT SIMPLY A CHURCH BUILDING A HOUSE FOR RELIGIOUS ASSEMBLY
transcript: To the fervent latter-day saint, a temple is not simply a church building, a house for religious assembly.

reference: SOON THOUSANDS OF CONVERTS HAD RENTED OR PURCHASED HOMES IN MISSOURI INDEPENDENCE JACKSON COUNTY BEING THEIR CENTER BUT FROM THE FIRST THEY WERE UNPOPULAR AMONG THE MISSOURIANS
transcript: Soon thousands of converts had rented or purchased homes in Missouri, Independence, Jackson County, being their center, but from the first they were unpopular among the Missourians.

reference: THE LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR LILBURN W BOGGS AFTERWARD GOVERNOR WAS A PRONOUNCED MORMON HATER AND THROUGHOUT THE PERIOD OF THE TROUBLES HE MANIFESTED SYMPATHY WITH THE PERSECUTORS
transcript: The lieutenant governor, little burnt W. Boggs, afterward governor, was a pronounced Mormon hater, and throughout the period of the troubles, he manifests his sympathy with the persecutors.

reference: THEIR SUFFERINGS HAVE NEVER YET BEEN FITLY CHRONICLED BY HUMAN SCRIBE
transcript: Their sufferings have never yet been fitly chronicled by human scribe.

reference: MAKING THEIR WAY ACROSS THE RIVER MOST OF THE REFUGEES FOUND SHELTER AMONG THE MORE HOSPITABLE PEOPLE OF CLAY COUNTY AND AFTERWARD ESTABLISHED THEMSELVES IN CALDWELL COUNTY THEREIN FOUNDING THE CITY OF FAR WEST
transcript: Making their way across the river, most of the refugees found shelter among the more hospitable people of Clay County, and afterward established themselves in Caldwell County, therein founding the city of Far West.

reference: A SMALL SETTLEMENT HAD BEEN FOUNDED BY MORMON FAMILIES ON SHOAL CREEK AND HERE ON THE THIRTIETH OF OCTOBER EIGHTEEN THIRTY EIGHT A COMPANY OF TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY FELL UPON THE HAPLESS SETTLERS AND BUTCHERED A SCORE
transcript: A small settlement had been founded by Mormon families on Sholl Creek, and here on the thirtieth of October, eighteen thirty eight, a company of two hundred and forty fell upon the hapless settlers and butchered a score.

reference: BE IT SAID TO THE HONOR OF SOME OF THE OFFICERS ENTRUSTED WITH THE TERRIBLE COMMISSION THAT WHEN THEY LEARNED ITS TRUE SIGNIFICANCE THEY RESIGNED THEIR AUTHORITY RATHER THAN HAVE ANYTHING TO DO WITH WHAT THEY DESIGNATED A COLD BLOODED BUTCHERY
transcript: Bates said to the honor of some of the officers entrusted with a terrible commission that when they learned its true significance, they resigned their authority rather than have anything to do with what they designated a cold-blooded butchery.

reference: OH WHAT A RECORD TO READ WHAT A PICTURE TO GAZE UPON HOW AWFUL THE FACT
transcript: Oh, what a record to read. What a picture to gaze upon. How awful the fact.

reference: AMERICAN SCHOOL BOYS READ WITH EMOTIONS OF HORROR OF THE ALBIGENSES DRIVEN BEATEN AND KILLED WITH A PAPAL LEGATE DIRECTING THE BUTCHERY AND OF THE VAUDOIS HUNTED AND HOUNDED LIKE BEASTS AS THE EFFECT OF A ROYAL DECREE AND THEY YET SHALL READ IN THE HISTORY OF THEIR OWN COUNTRY OF SCENES AS TERRIBLE AS THESE IN THE EXHIBITION OF INJUSTICE AND INHUMAN HATE
transcript: American schoolboys read with emotions of horror of the Albigenses, driven, beaten and killed with a papal legate directing the butchery, and of the fodois, hunted and hounded like beasts, as the effect of a royal decree, and they yet shall read in the history of their own country of scenes as terrible as these in the exhibition of injustice and inhuman hate.

reference: WHO BEGAN THE QUARREL WAS IT THE MORMONS
transcript: Who began the quarrel? Was it the Mormons?

reference: AS A SAMPLE OF THE PRESS COMMENTS AGAINST THE BRUTALITY OF THE MISSOURIANS I QUOTE A PARAGRAPH FROM THE QUINCY ARGUS MARCH SIXTEENTH EIGHTEEN THIRTY NINE
transcript: As the sample of the press comments against the brutality of the Missourians, I quote a paragraph from the Quincy Argus, March sixteenth, eighteen thirty nine.

reference: IT WILL BE OBSERVED THAT AN ORGANIZED MOB AIDED BY MANY OF THE CIVIL AND MILITARY OFFICERS OF MISSOURI WITH GOVERNOR BOGGS AT THEIR HEAD HAVE BEEN THE PROMINENT ACTORS IN THIS BUSINESS INCITED TOO IT APPEARS AGAINST THE MORMONS BY POLITICAL HATRED AND BY THE ADDITIONAL MOTIVES OF PLUNDER AND REVENGE
transcript: It will be observed that an organized mob aided by many of the civil and military officers of Missouri, with governor bogs at their head, have been the prominent actors in this business, incited to it appears against the Mormons by political hatred, and by the additional motives of plunder and revenge.

reference: THE ARMY FOUND THE PEOPLE IN POVERTY AND LEFT THEM IN COMPARATIVE WEALTH
transcript: The army found the people in poverty and left them in comparative wealth.

reference: BUT A WORD FURTHER CONCERNING THE EXPEDITION IN GENERAL
transcript: But a word further concerning the expedition in general.

reference: IT WAS THROUGH FLOYD'S ADVICE THAT BUCHANAN ORDERED THE MILITARY EXPEDITION TO UTAH OSTENSIBLY TO INSTALL CERTAIN FEDERAL OFFICIALS AND TO REPRESS AN ALLEGED INFANTILE REBELLION WHICH IN FACT HAD NEVER COME INTO EXISTENCE BUT IN REALITY TO FURTHER THE INTERESTS OF THE SECESSIONISTS
transcript: It was through Floyd's advice that Buchanan ordered the military expedition to Utah, ostensibly to install certain federal officials and to repress an alleged infantile rebellion, which in fact had never come into existence, but in reality to further the interests of the secessionists.

reference: MOREOVER HAD THE PEOPLE BEEN INCLINED TO REBELLION WHAT GREATER OPPORTUNITY COULD THEY HAVE WISHED
transcript: Moreover, had the people been inclined to rebellion, while greater opportunity could they have wished.

reference: ALREADY A NORTH AND A SOUTH WERE TALKED OF WHY NOT SET UP ALSO A WEST
transcript: Already in north and south were talked of, Why not set up also a west?

reference: THEY KNEW NO NORTH NO SOUTH NO EAST NO WEST THEY STOOD POSITIVELY BY THE CONSTITUTION AND WOULD HAVE NOTHING TO DO IN THE BLOODY STRIFE BETWEEN BROTHERS UNLESS INDEED THEY WERE SUMMONED BY THE AUTHORITY TO WHICH THEY HAD ALREADY ONCE LOYALLY RESPONDED TO FURNISH MEN AND ARMS FOR THEIR COUNTRY'S NEED
transcript: They knew no north, no south, no east, no west. They stood positively by the Constitution, and would have nothing to do in the bloody strife between brothers. Unless indeed they were summoned by the authority to which they had already once loyally responded to furnishment and arms for the country's need.

reference: WHAT THE LATTER DAY SAINTS CALL CELESTIAL MARRIAGE IS CHARACTERISTIC OF THE CHURCH AND IS IN VERY GENERAL PRACTISE BUT OF CELESTIAL MARRIAGE PLURALITY OF WIVES WAS AN INCIDENT NEVER AN ESSENTIAL
transcript: What the latter naysayings call celestial marriage is characteristic of the church and is in very general practice, but of celestial marriage, plurality of wives was an incident, never an essential.

reference: WE BELIEVE IN A LITERAL RESURRECTION AND AN ACTUAL HEREAFTER IN WHICH FUTURE STATE SHALL BE RECOGNIZED EVERY SANCTIFIED AND AUTHORIZED RELATIONSHIP EXISTING HERE ON EARTH OF PARENT AND CHILD BROTHER AND SISTER HUSBAND AND WIFE
transcript: We believe in a literal resurrection and an actual hereafter, in which future states shall be recognized every sanctified and authorized relationship existing here on earth, of parent and child, brother and sister, husband and wife.

reference: IT HAS BEEN MY PRIVILEGE TO TREAD THE SOIL OF MANY LANDS TO OBSERVE THE CUSTOMS AND STUDY THE HABITS OF MORE NATIONS THAN ONE AND I HAVE YET TO FIND THE PLACE AND MEET THE PEOPLE WHERE AND WITH WHOM THE PURITY OF MAN AND WOMAN IS HELD MORE PRECIOUS THAN AMONG THE MALIGNED MORMONS IN THE MOUNTAIN VALLEYS OF THE WEST
transcript: It has been my privilege to tread the soil of many lands, to observe the customs and study the habits of more nations than one. Nive yet to find the place and meet the people, wherein with whom the purity of man and woman is held more precious than among the malignant and the mountain valleys of the West.

reference: AT THE INCEPTION OF PLURAL MARRIAGE AMONG THE LATTER DAY SAINTS THERE WAS NO LAW NATIONAL OR STATE AGAINST ITS PRACTISE
